q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: WITH Bar_Drinkers AS (SELECT f.bar, COUNT(f.drinker) AS total_num_drinker FROM frequents AS f GROUP BY f.bar), Avg_Bar_Price AS (SELECT s.bar, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price FROM serves AS s GROUP BY s.bar), Max_Visits AS (SELECT f.drinker, MAX(f.times_a_week) AS highest_visits FROM frequents AS f GROUP BY f.drinker), Most_Freq_Drinker AS (SELECT f.bar, f.drinker AS most_reg_drinker FROM frequents AS f JOIN Max_Visits AS mv ON f.drinker = mv.drinker AND f.times_a_week = mv.highest_visits) SELECT b.name, bd.total_num_drinker, abp.avg_price, mfd.most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN Bar_Drinkers AS bd ON b.name = bd.bar LEFT JOIN Avg_Bar_Price AS abp ON b.name = abp.bar LEFT JOIN Most_Freq_Drinker AS mfd ON b.name = mfd.bar ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the way they handle the subquery for the most regular drinker. Q1 orders the subquery results by times_a_week DESC and drinker ASC, while Q2 orders by highest_visits DESC and drinker ASC. This difference can lead to different results when there are ties in the number of visits.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have two bars, 'B1' and 'B2', each with two regular drinkers, 'D1' and 'D2', who visit 'B1' and 'B2' the same number of times a week. 'D1' lives closer to 'B1' than 'D2' lives to 'B2', but 'D2' lives closer to 'B2' than 'D1' lives to 'B1'.
